review_type: UI default-state code and browser-evidence review; prior v9 mechanical geometry review retained by unchanged model fingerprints
environment: Local Windows; current PNG files inspected with view_image; source coordinates and SHA-256 inspected directly
viewing_scope: This UI round visually inspected the fresh browser rear-view screenshot and read the current UI source plus the executed browser report/checker. Prior adult component state images remain applicable because all recorded model, rig and animation fingerprints are unchanged.

acceptance_checks.evidence: The front component is not visible in either retracted image. Half and full extension progressively expose the component without a visible gap at its root.

The exported maximum component width is 0.40092048 units, approximately 9.28 percent of the 4.32-unit body width. The 0.36 scale follows 4.32/12. At full extension, the root rear boundary is z=-1.4348, leaving 0.0452 units inside the body front plane at z=-1.48. Final preferred size remains for user confirmation.

The rear retractable marker is invisible at rest and midpoint in both species. At full extension a small surface marker becomes visible without a detached backing panel. The fixed rear marker remains visible throughout.

At the component center, the rest marker plane is 0.088 units inside the rear surface; a 0.10-unit travel places the fully extended marker approximately 0.012 units outside it. Rotation follows the local rear slope, while the base remains embedded.

The current general views retain the joined lower body, temple coverage, visible fixed rear marker, exposed Reimu ribbon tails and Marisa brim contact. The retracted rear component no longer protrudes in side view.

findings.finding: Gold crown hair protrudes above Marisa's lowered brim, along the hat band and accessory base.
findings.required_action: Keep the hair crown underneath the hat while preserving broad contact between brim and hair. Re-render front, three-quarter, side and back views.

findings.finding: Both back views show thin bright dashed seams on the left and right skin shoulders immediately below the hair hem.
findings.evidence: In reimu-back.png at 640x640, approximately x132-188 and x453-506, y424; the same defect appears on Marisa.
findings.required_action: Close the skin section boundary or remove coplanar exposed edges, then verify that the bright seams disappear in the new back views. The exact geometric cause has not yet been isolated.

findings.finding: The wider cheeks hide most of the short side-lock tips, leaving small dark or gold blocks below the ties in front view.
findings.required_action: Consider a small outward or forward side-lock adjustment so the short tied locks remain readable against the wider body. Preserve the requested short hair length.

visual_assessment: The lower belly is visibly wider than the upper face region, with a rounded lower edge rather than the pointed lower silhouette of v5.
Front, three-quarter and side views show the face skin continuing into the belly; no detached face plate is visible.
The side and rear hair wrap around the head and terminate above the lower belly. Reimu bow roots meet the rear crown in the inspected static views.
No blocking visual defect was found in the eight neutral turnaround views. This is an agent visual review, not user approval of the standard design.

resolved_findings.evidence: All four Marisa views show the gold crown below the brim, with no gold hair protruding into the hat band or accessory base. The brim is supported by a broad hair layer.
Both back views now show uninterrupted skin shoulders beneath the hair; the bright dashed seams seen in review 1 are absent.
The tied side locks show short exposed tips, particularly in three-quarter views, after the outward and forward placement adjustment.

history.user_followup: The user subsequently requested less pronounced horizontal stacking on the lower front belly.

history.reason: The earlier v7 assessment relied too heavily on reduced front shading bands. Subsequent user feedback and reinspection found genuine stepped corner edges, partially buried Reimu bow tails, and an obscured rear marker. The earlier ready decision is not current evidence.

history.finding: The shared-vertex body fixed the abdominal ledges, but a new exposed skin wedge appeared behind the side lock in Reimu side view.
history.bow_root_followup: A small dark notch was investigated using exported coordinates. Adjacent root segments overlapped in depth by approximately 0.1903 units and their exterior remained beyond the hair surface; the notch was a contour gap, not demonstrated hair penetration.

acceptance_checks.evidence: Front, three-quarter and low front closeups show a connected lower shell. The former horizontal shelves, stepped corner caps and small fragmented surface shadows are absent. Normal shading at the broad bottom bevel remains and is not being described as a mathematically smooth surface.

The large skin wedge behind the side lock seen in v8-review-1 is now covered. Front, three-quarter and waddle images show complete eyes and cheeks with no new temple-panel occlusion or detached face panel.

Bow closeup, rear-quarter and rear views show both red tails and their light hems outside the hair. The root segments remain connected; the small dark side notches correspond to the root silhouette rather than demonstrated penetration of the exposed red surface.
Both rear, rear-quarter and rear closeup views show the marker on the body surface. No large rectangular backing plate or detached patch is visible.
Marisa front, side, rear, closeup and waddle images retain brim-to-hair contact without gold crown hair above the brim.
One waddle pose per species was viewed at the manifest time of 0.24 seconds; the face, temple panels and accessories remain attached in these images. This is not a full-cycle visual acceptance test.

limitations: This round evaluates mechanical fit and relative dimensions of adult model components, not a user-approved standard proportion.
The three rendered states sample the extension clip at the times in the manifest; they do not establish full-cycle visual acceptance under every locomotion or expression combination.
The body uses shared-vertex mesh with legacy poly_mesh interchange export; Minecraft/GeckoLib runtime adaptation and acceptance remain pending.
The UI browser checks cover the reported subject modes and reset actions; they do not establish all history/cache restoration scenarios or all juvenile lifecycle frames.

ui_state_review.visual_evidence: The fresh browser screenshot shows the fixed rear marker alone, with no independent retractable mark below it.
code_findings_resolved: resetAnatomy retracts and immediately sets amount to zero before repaint; subject changes, action changes, restart and restore use this path.
The UI explicitly displays the retracted, extending, extended, retracting or switching state.
The preview wrapper passes the first twelve characters of the inner page content hash as its iframe rev query.

browser_evidence.reviewer_action: Read the executed report and checker source, verified their artifact fingerprints, and inspected the resulting browser screenshot; did not rerun the browser checker independently.
browser_evidence.precise_pixel_check_scope: The checker removes anatomy geometry from DATA.characters only while viewing six subject modes at time zero from the rear. It does not remove ordinaryCharacters anatomy, and it does not exercise hatched juveniles; the empty nest mode at time zero is not juvenile pixel-visibility evidence.

ui_state_review.supporting_read_only_analysis: Fresh controller state begins at zero extension. Juveniles use empty overrides and uniform model scaling, preserving the embedded component relation. Ordinary reference geometry had its rear component about 0.835 units behind the rear body surface in the inspected default data.
